messages:
mike: hey folks — need quick help. My mom was prescribed a 10-day IV antibiotic at home next week. Is home infusion nursing covered under Redwood Choice PPO? Also will a photo of the digital ID card be enough for the vendor to bill?

sara (People Ops): hi mike — sorry to hear, hope she feels better. Short answer: usually yes, but depends on medical necessity + prior auth. If the order is for home health nursing, the vendor needs an authorization number from our insurer. A digital ID photo is usually OK for proof of coverage, but the vendor may ask for member ID + group number printed clearly.

mike: ok thanks. how do we start the prior auth? vendor said they can submit, or we can have the clinic do it. which is faster?

sara (People Ops): vendor can submit but fastest is clinic + vendor in parallel. Steps: 1) clinic uploads physician order to insurer portal (include dx and estimated visits), 2) vendor submits clinical intake and request for home infusion nursing with the same order, 3) insurer issues auth code. I recommend the clinic start today and vendor follow up.

mike: any specific docs to attach?

sara (People Ops): yes — attach: physician order (signed), plan of care, estimated visit schedule, med details (dose/frequency), and superbill if available. Also include member's full name and DOB. If you want, paste a copy of the front of the digital ID card and the member number.

raj: vendor-facing tip — if the vendor is out-of-network, ask for an estimate and ask if they’ll do a direct-bill or if you need to file an out-of-network claim. Sometimes trying an in-network home health agency prevents surprise charges.

mike: vendor is local "BrightHome Care" — not sure if they're in-network. where do I check network quickly?

sara (People Ops): quickest: benefits.redwood.com -> "Find a Provider" and search for home health / infusion nursing. If the vendor isn't listed, ask vendor for NPI and call the insurer provider line to verify. If you want, DM me the NPI and I'll check.

benefits-bot: automated note — Prior auth typical turnaround: 3–5 business days. For urgent/expedited requests (within 72 hours), call provider line and ask for expedited review. Keep authorization confirmation (screen shot or auth letter) in case of later claim issues.

mike: perfect. one more — is there a template or short email I can send vendor/clinic so we don't miss anything?

sara (People Ops): yes — use this short template copy/paste: 

```
Subject: Prior Auth Request for Home Infusion Nursing — [Member Name]

Hi [Vendor/Clinic],

Please submit a prior auth for home infusion nursing for [Member Name] (DOB: [MM/DD/YYYY], Member ID: [########]). Attached: signed physician order, plan of care, med administration instructions. Diagnosis: [ICD-10]. Estimated visits: [#]. Please send authorization number and estimated start date to [mike@email.com] and upload approval to insurer portal.

Thanks,
[Your Name]
```

mike: really helpful, thanks! DMing you the vendor NPI now.

linda: fwiw — save screenshots of any auth number the insurer gives over the phone. We had a case where the authorization wasn't linked to claim and screenshot saved the day. :+1:

sara (People Ops): great point linda. mike — if anything gets denied, forward the denial to people-ops@redwood.com and we can help with appeals or getting the vendor to resubmit with correct codes. Good luck! :hugging_face:
